item.title: What Happens After You Send a Message in an LLM Chat UI
item.description:
A chat interface makes an interaction with a large language model look simple: type a message, press Enter, and watch an answer appear. Behind that interaction is a distributed request pipeline involving the browser, application servers, databases, policy systems, model gateways, inference workers, and often tools or retrieval services.

In an existing conversation, the new text is only one part of the model’s input. The application must reconstruct enough of the conversation, combine it with hidden instructions and other context, fit everything into a finite context window, run inference, stream the result, and persist the new state.

item.title: Measuring Browser and DOM Dimensions
item.description:
Browser APIs expose several coordinate systems because a screen, browser window, viewport, document, and element answer different measurement questions. Choosing an API by name alone can therefore produce scrollbar, rounding, or scrolling errors.

Window, Screen, and Viewport Measurements #

API Measurement
window.innerWidth, innerHeight Layout viewport, including a rendered classic scrollbar
window.outerWidth, outerHeight Browser window’s outside dimensions
screen.width, screen.height Screen dimensions in CSS pixels
screen.availWidth, screen.availHeight Screen space excluding reserved operating-system areas
document.documentElement.clientWidth, clientHeight Layout viewport excluding a classic scrollbar

CSS pixels are logical units. A CSS pixel can cover multiple device pixels on a high-density display, so screen.width does not necessarily equal the panel’s physical pixel count.

item.description: CSS is organized as a standards family, not as a single versioned language. The specification evolves in levels and modules, while browsers implement a moving subset of those documents.

item.title: Implementing Light and Dark Color Schemes
item.description:
A color-scheme implementation needs three layers:

  1. A system preference used when the visitor has made no site-specific choice.
  2. An explicit site preference that can override the system.
  3. Semantic colors that keep components independent from literal light and dark values.

Declare Semantic Colors #

Name variables by role rather than by appearance:

css 
:root {
 color-scheme: light dark;
 --surface: #ffffff;
 --surface-raised: #f5f6f8;
 --text: #17191c;
 --text-muted: #5d6470;
 --border: #d7dbe0;
 --accent: #1659b7;
}

body {
 color: var(--text);
 background: var(--surface);
}

color-scheme tells the user agent which schemes the page supports, allowing form controls, scrollbars, and system colors to match. It does not define the site’s custom palette.

item.title: Spring MVC
item.description:
Spring MVC is the Servlet-based web framework in Spring Framework. Its front controller, DispatcherServlet, coordinates request mapping, argument resolution, controller invocation, return-value handling, and exception translation. Spring WebFlux uses a different reactive runtime and threading model; the two frameworks must not be treated as interchangeable.

Bootstrap and Dispatch #

A non-Boot Servlet application can register a web application context and dispatcher through WebApplicationInitializer:

java 
public final class WebInitializer implements WebApplicationInitializer {
 @Override
 public void onStartup(ServletContext servletContext) {
 var context = new AnnotationConfigWebApplicationContext();
 context.register(WebConfiguration.class);

 var servlet = servletContext.addServlet(
 "mvc", new DispatcherServlet(context));
 servlet.setLoadOnStartup(1);
 servlet.addMapping("/");
 }
}

Spring Boot performs equivalent registration for an MVC application. Mapping the dispatcher to / lets the Servlet container retain special handling for static resources and JSPs; /* also captures those dispatches.

item.title: Browser Content Disposition and Downloads
item.description:
Browsers decide whether to display a response, download it, or hand it to an external application from several inputs. Content-Disposition provides a strong preference, but content type, navigation context, sandboxing, browser capabilities, and user settings also affect the result.

Inline and Attachment Dispositions #

An attachment response requests a download:

http 
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/pdf
Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="guide.pdf"
Content-Length: 110352
X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff

An inline response permits presentation inside the browser:

http 
Content-Type: application/pdf
Content-Disposition: inline; filename="guide.pdf"

inline does not guarantee display. The browser needs a viewer for the media type, and the user can configure some types to download instead. Omitting the header leaves the choice primarily to the media type and navigation context.

item.title: The CSS Box Model
item.description:
CSS lays out each element as one or more boxes. A basic box contains, from the inside outward, content, padding, border, and margin. Width calculations become predictable only after identifying which edge a declared size controls.

Content and Border Sizing #

The initial box-sizing value is content-box:

css 
.card {
 box-sizing: content-box;
 width: 20rem;
 padding: 1rem;
 border: 0.25rem solid;
}

The rendered border-box width is 22.5rem: 20 rem of content, 2 rem of horizontal padding, and 0.5 rem of border.

item.title: Responsive CSS and Layout
item.description:
Responsive layout should derive from content constraints instead of a list of device models. Intrinsic sizing, flexbox, grid, media queries, and container queries provide complementary controls.

Establish a Responsive Foundation #

The viewport declaration makes the CSS viewport match the device width:

html 
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">

Do not add user-scalable=no or a low maximum-scale; page zoom is an accessibility mechanism. Applications that position controls around an on-screen keyboard may also need the visual viewport API, because the visible area can change without the layout viewport changing.

item.title: Browser Platform, Graphics, and Playwright in Docker
item.description:
Browser automation succeeds when tests model document loading, layout, networking, and rendering rather than treating a page as a static string.

Measure the Browser and DOM #

Browser dimensions answer different questions:

API Measurement
window.innerWidth and innerHeight Layout viewport, including a rendered scrollbar
window.outerWidth and outerHeight Browser window bounds
screen.width and screen.height Screen dimensions in CSS pixels
screen.availWidth and availHeight Screen space excluding reserved operating-system areas
element.clientWidth and clientHeight Content box plus padding, excluding border and scrollbar
element.scrollWidth and scrollHeight Scrollable content extent
element.offsetWidth and offsetHeight Border-box dimensions, rounded to integer pixels
element.getBoundingClientRect() Border-box geometry in viewport coordinates, retaining fractions

clientWidth is zero for an inline element without a layout box. On the root element, it describes the layout viewport without a classic scrollbar. Avoid mixing viewport coordinates from getBoundingClientRect() with document coordinates without adding the scroll offset.

item.title: Browser Authentication
item.description:
Browser authentication assigns an application request to a user or workload identity. The application must define where credentials reside, which requests carry them, how the browser restricts them, and how the server invalidates them.

Sessions and Cookies #

For a browser application with a same-site backend, an opaque session identifier in a cookie keeps the credential out of JavaScript. Store session state server-side, rotate the identifier after authentication and privilege changes, and expire it on logout and inactivity.

item.title: Server-Driven HTTP Traffic
item.description:
Server-driven HTTP lets a server send information without a new client request for every update. Server-Sent Events (SSE) is a simple standardized option for one-way server-to-browser updates.

Server-Sent Events #

An SSE client makes a normal GET request with an Accept: text/event-stream header. The server replies with 200 OK, Content-Type: text/event-stream, and keeps the response open while sending UTF-8 event fields separated by a blank line:

text 
event: order-updated
id: 42
data: {"status":"paid"}

In browsers, EventSource reconnects automatically. The server can send retry: to suggest a reconnection delay, and the browser sends Last-Event-ID after a reconnect when an event ID was received. Design the stream so clients can resume from that ID or refresh a snapshot safely.
